prompts.uart_tx.sv: Solve the engineering task specified by spec.md. Return exactly ONE JSON object per turn, no prose or additional actions. Allowed actions: {"tool":"read","file":"spec.md"}, {"tool":"read","file":"uart_tx.sv"}, {"tool":"edit","content":"complete file"}, {"tool":"test"}, {"tool":"submit"}. Read both files before edit or submit. Only uart_tx.sv can be edited. Test runs the trusted public checker against the current file. You have at most 20 total actions and 4 public tests. Rejected actions also consume an action. Submission is allowed without passing tests and ends solving. Independent terminal and held-out results are not returned. No shell, other files, reference, checker or private inputs are available. Do not combine actions.

stopping_rules: Stop remaining cohort on source drift, isolation failure or indeterminate trusted checker. Preserve all started attempts; no replacements.
Each trial ends on submit, 20 actions, worker error or1200seconds.
primary_questions: Can different deliverable types be solved through the same four-action boundary?
Are independent correctness and defect-detection obligations satisfied?
Does public success generalize to fixed terminal and separate evaluation checks?

offline_analysis.reserved_evaluation: After solver stop, separately retained; never used for training selection
offline_analysis.first_candidate: Only actual observed tests; do not retrospectively label untested candidates

estimated_resources.basis: UART13controls plus4phasechecks actually completed; stimulus10checks with one shared trusted-bank compile completed; formal4realtrials show modest request counts but do not predict UART repair

interpretation: One trial per contract, exploratory task calibration, not success-rate estimation or a controlled cross-task tool-effect comparison.
controller_acceptance_scope: Real session-v2 test budget/submit boundary, isolated installed worker probe, and unit tests. Runner multi-deliverable prompt selection is a deployment adapter; current code frozen and each real execution audited.
